name: Auckland Airport

slots.v: general aviation and business aviation need a valid landing and/or parking slot during declared peak congestion periods; flying without one can mean a ban from those periods for at least 30 days
slots.quote: without first obtaining a valid landing and/or parking slot during periods of peak congestion

handling.v: operators must self-handle (with the airport's written consent and licence) or appoint a third-party ground handling agent
handling.quote: You are required to either self handle, or appoint third party ground handling agents.

runway.v: runway 05R/23L is 3,635 m long and 75 m wide including shoulders, Code F capable (operator's draft master plan; AIP declared distances not read)
runway.quote: Runway 05R/23L measures 3,635 metres by 75 metres (including shoulders) and is capable of handling Code F aircraft.

customs.v: not open-ended: non-scheduled and private flights must arrive during Customs working hours unless there are extenuating circumstances; arriving outside them needs approval at least 5 working days ahead; the hours are not defined. Auckland is a listed Customs Place and Place of First Arrival
customs.quote: You must arrive during working hours unless there are extenuating circumstances.

ppr.v: non-scheduled general aviation flights need specific written permission from the airport company, and an authorised ground handler (CAA booklet, revised March 2023)
ppr.quote: Non-scheduled operations by general aviation aircraft require specific written permission from the airport company

permits.v: a foreign charter needs a New Zealand Foreign Air Operator's Certificate under CAR Part 129 (allow up to 90 days), unless it is a single landing and single take-off within any 28 days
permits.quote: they are classified as Air Transport Operations (ATO) and require certification under Civil Aviation Rule (CAR) 129. ... Permitted is a single landing and a single takeoff within any 28-day period without any certification.

notes: 1 Nov 2026: added slots (clause 5.7) and handling (clause 6.1) from Auckland Airport's Conditions of Use effective 30 Oct 2022 (the current version on corporate.aucklandairport.co.nz). The Conditions of Use state no hours, no curfew and no aircraft size limits (clause 7.1 sets minimum insurance by MTOW, from USD 30M up to 10,000 kg). Auckland Airport's noise page mentions only a 10 dB night weighting (22:00-07:00) for noise measurement, not a flight restriction. Not opened (permission not granted in time): NZ AIP https://www.aip.net.nz/, https://www.aip.net.nz/assets/AIP/Aerodromes-AD1/AERODROMES/NZAA_AD2.pdf and http://www.aip.net.nz/NavWalk.aspx?section=CHARTS. Runway, curfew, customs and hours still need the AIP. 28 Oct 2026: AIP and CAA NZ AIP index were blocked. | 3 Nov 2026: Customs also wants passenger details and Form C1A at least 3 hours before departure, and at least 2 hours' (preferably 24 hours') notice before leaving; levies are on the page (updated 18 Jul 2025). The CAA page also says a Ministry air services licence is needed, conditional on the certificate. Curfew and aerodrome hours still not found: the airport's general information page gives terminal hours only (international terminal 24 hours), which are not recorded as a rule. NZ AIP: AD2 PDF refused https://www.aip.net.nz/assets/AIP/Aerodromes-AD1/AERODROMES/NZAA_AD2.pdf, and the chart PDF https://www.aip.net.nz/assets/AIP/Aerodrome-Charts/Auckland-NZAA/NZAA_53.04_53.05.pdf returned only the site's conditions of use (a click-through page), so the owner has to download them. 5 Nov 2026: nothing new. Searches for curfew or 24-hour wording on the airport's sites surfaced investor presentations (2018, 2023 and 2024) and the ANCCG noise glossary, all of which failed at the site; the 2025 master plan summary was refused this run. None of these was read, so curfew stays missing. | 7 Nov 2026: nothing new. NZ AIP AD 2 still not readable: https://www.aip.net.nz/ PDFs return only the site's conditions-of-use click-through page (tested with NZWN_AD2.pdf), and direct download of NZAA_AD2.pdf was refused by the network proxy (403). Auckland Airport general information page (international terminal open 24 hours) gives terminal hours only; FY24 Annual Aircraft Noise Report (22 Nov 2024) defines night as 22:00-07:00 for noise reporting but states no curfew; Auckland Unitary Plan (July 2026) Designation 1100 sets Northern Runway night conditions (non-jet aircraft 22:00-07:00 not to depart to or arrive from the east; wide-body jets not to depart west 22:00-07:00 for the first five years) but the Northern Runway is not yet built and no airport curfew is stated. Curfew, hours and IATA stay missing. Unitary Plan HTML page https://unitaryplan.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/HTMLSept/Part 7/Auckland International Airport Ltd.htm failed at its site.
